title: Sparrowline Renewal - Onramp & Capacity Stretch Review
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on adding APAC (Japan) region and a short-term capacity stretch for peak season. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, latency/cost targets, KMS and SOC2 questions, pilot timeline, and pricing cadence. Agreed to run a 4-week pilot with regional staging and internal benchmark; Redwood to send SOW draft + security pack.
action_items: Redwood (Luis) - provide Japan region perf benchmark spreadsheet by 2028-03-24
Redwood (Maya) - send draft SOW and pilot pricing tiers by 2028-03-22
Customer (Tom) - share current infra metrics (p99, avg token size, daily tokens) by 2028-03-21
Customer (Mei) - list security/compliance checklist items (KMS, auditors) by 2028-03-23
next_steps: Schedule kickoff for 4-week pilot w/ staging on Japan region (target start 2028-03-29)
Redwood to share security pack + SOC2 cert + data flow diagram
Agree on success criteria (p99 < 250ms; cost per 1k tokens target) and measurement plan
meeting_header:
Date: 2028-03-19 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Diane Park (CSM); Jordan Reyes (CTO, Sparrowline), Anika Bose (Head of ML), Tom Greenwood (Infra Lead), Mei Tan (Security)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can start, we got 45ish minutes on the calendar, so quick intros.
00:12 Jordan Reyes: yeah thanks maya, jordan here, anika, tom and mei on our side. we wanted to focus on the renewal plus a short term capacity stretch for our Q2 campaign, and the APAC region onboarding.
00:25 Luis Ortega: sounds great—i'm luis from the se team. quick clarifying q: when you say APAC, are we talking full data residency in japan or just region routing?
00:38 Anika Bose: our product team needs requests to originate and be served in jp-east for latency, and for legal we need logs retained in-country for a subset of workloads. not full sovereign stack yet but leaning that direction.
00:52 Tom Greenwood: on the capacity, last year we saw a 3x spike during the promo window, so we need burst, not necessarily a permanent 3x commit.
01:05 Maya Chen: okay understood. we can do a mix—dedicated reserved for baseline and burst in hosted or dedicated-burst. tradeoffs are cost vs guaranteed throughput.
01:18 Mei Tan: we'd also like to know KMS options—can you integrate with our HSM, and do you provide audit logs that are parsed for our SIEM?
01:30 Luis Ortega: yes on KMS—Redwood private can use customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM integrations. audit logs are available with fielded events; we'll share sample log schema. (note: sometimes the transcription shows that as "K V cash" in our auto-gen)
01:45 Jordan Reyes: perfect. can you walk through a sample architecture for japan region? where does the control plane live?
01:55 Diane Park: control plane remains in Redwood's control plane by default; for private deployments we provide a customer-managed control plane option. for this engagement i think we should scope a partial private control plane for the jp pilot to reduce data egress.
02:12 Anika Bose: quick qual question—what models are you recommending? we are using a mix of open LLMs quantized on gpus.
02:22 Luis Ortega: for low-latency chat we'd recommend a 4-bit quantized variant of the model with batching tuned to your seq length distribution; we can map workloads to different model variants. also can fallback to a cheaper distil model for non-critical calls.
02:35 Tom Greenwood: our average prompt length is 180 tokens but p99 is like 1,200 when users paste long context. how does that affect batching?
02:46 Luis Ortega: long tails do reduce batching efficiency; we can set separate routes for short/medium/long contexts and have different batching windows. that keeps p99 down for short queries.
02:58 Jordan Reyes: are there any penalties or cost cliffs if we do regional burst? we don't want surprise bills.
03:10 Maya Chen: good point—billing has dedicated base plus burst capping options. we'll propose a guardrail—burst budget thresholds + alerts and auto-fallback to hosted cheaper model if burst exceeds tiers.
03:24 Anika Bose: on the SLA, our product requires p99 < 250ms for short queries; do you think that's realistic in jp region?
03:35 Luis Ortega: depends on hardware and routing; with dedicated gp100-ish (note: transcription might say "G one hundred") nodes and tuned kernels, yes for short contexts. long contexts will be higher. we'll run microbenchmarks.
03:48 Tom Greenwood: can you do a benchmark against our current baseline? we run on-prem inference with our own pipeline yielding p99 ~300ms for short cases.
03:59 Luis Ortega: absolutely, please share your sample traces and we'll run a like-for-like bench in jp staging. we estimate we can get to 200-230ms p99 with dedicated and prefix caching.
04:15 Jordan Reyes: caching—how is KV cache handled? we need to ensure cache keying respects PII rules.
04:25 Luis Ortega: KV cache respects the tenant id and redaction rules; by default we recommend prefix caching and we support sticky routing to keep KV local to region. note: the automated text sometimes shows that as "K V cash" or "K V catch" but the config is explicit.
04:40 Mei Tan: security—SOC2 is fine but do you have auditors that can do my team a run-through? we use a third-party auditor.
04:50 Diane Park: we have SOC2 Type II and can share attestations and the standard answer pack. for deeper audits we can coordinate with our security partnerships; we'll add contact in the packet.
05:05 Jordan Reyes: ok good. pricing model question: our finance team wants a predictable monthly commit with tiered burst rather than per-token wildcards.
05:18 Maya Chen: we typically structure dedicated as commit + burst credits; we can build a model that maps to your forecast with a smoothing discount. i'll send a draft SOW and pricing tiers.
05:30 Anika Bose: i'd like to lock down success criteria for the pilot—what do we measure to call it a win?
05:39 Maya Chen: propose: 1) p99 < 250ms for short route measured over 2 weeks; 2) burst handling with < 5% error rate during simulated peak; 3) cost per 1k tokens improvement vs your current baseline by at least 10%.
05:55 Jordan Reyes: that sounds reasonable. will you instrument cost and latency tracing by token?
06:04 Luis Ortega: yes, tracing is token-level and we can export to your prometheus/grafana or provide our dashboard access.
06:12 Tom Greenwood: on the timeline, we want JP region live for a small beta by mid-april; is that feasible?
06:22 Maya Chen: aiming for pilot start 2028-03-29 gives two weeks for staging and internal validation; if SOW and infra paperwork get done this week it's feasible.
06:33 Mei Tan: paperwork includes DPA updates and the KMS integration checklist—i'll need to run those by legal.
06:41 Maya Chen: we'll include a DPA redline and KMS flow in the security pack.
06:47 Anika Bose: competitors—we're also talking to ApexInference who offered a lower commit but not sure on SOC2 maturity. any notes on differentiators?
06:58 Maya Chen: Redwood's differentiator is production-first tooling—token-level tracing, fallback policies, and a unified contract for hosted/dedicated/private. price-performance we'll show via bench results.
07:12 Jordan Reyes: curious, what about data residency—if logs must stay in-country can you guarantee that?
07:21 Diane Park: yes we can keep logs in region for scoped workloads via our private deployment option; for hosted we can also provide region-retained logs but the control plane remains outside unless we do private control plane.
07:36 Tom Greenwood: can you summarize the options in an architecture diagram? a simple flow would help get internal signoffs.
07:44 Luis Ortega: we'll add a network/data flow diagram in the pack—showing hosts, KMS handoff, control plane, and where auditing hooks live.
07:54 Maya Chen: action items recap: luis will run perf benchmarks and share spreadsheet; maya will send SOW + pricing; tom will send infra metrics; mei will send security checklist items; target: pilot kickoff week of 2028-03-29.
08:09 Jordan Reyes: yes, and include an option for a 4-week pilot with a 1-month extension clause for safety.
08:17 Maya Chen: absolutely. any other blockers?
08:21 Anika Bose: one small note: our ML team may require a model-variant with deterministic outputs for evaluation; do you support pinned model versions and rollbacks?
08:31 Luis Ortega: yes model pinning, rollbacks, and A/B rollout policies are supported. we'll include example configs.
08:40 Tom Greenwood: network egress—what's the expected egress pattern? we might need to open dedicated peering.
08:47 Diane Park: we can recommend peering or private link depending on throughput; we'll outline costs and expected latency improvements.
08:58 Jordan Reyes: okay that helps. pricing again: if we commit to a small dedicated baseline + burst, what does the minimum contractual term look like?
09:07 Maya Chen: standard is quarterly minimum for dedicated, but pilot terms can be 4 weeks with an option to roll into quarterly commit; we'll reflect that in SOW.
09:17 Anika Bose: can we get a quick walkthrough of the console and cost UI in the pilot?
09:23 Luis Ortega: yes we'll provision read-only console access and a cost dashboard for the pilot.
09:30 Mei Tan: last question—encryption in transit, do you provide mTLS for service-to-service in region?
09:36 Luis Ortega: yes mTLS and customer certs available for private deployments; hosted supports TLS with mutual auth for private links. we'll include specifics.
09:46 Jordan Reyes: all right that's everything i think. thanks team, any closing remarks?
09:52 Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll send the SOW + security pack by thursday (2028-03-22). luis will push perf results by friday (2028-03-24). tom to share metrics by tuesday (2028-03-21). mei to provide compliance items by thursday (2028-03-23).
10:09 Jordan Reyes: great, we'll review and aim to sign pilot by week of 3/29. thanks all.
10:15 END TRANSCRIPT

Notes on transcription: auto-captions occasionally mis-spell acronyms (KMS -> K M S, KV cache -> K V cash), and some proper names are approximated. The participants used informal shorthand (gp100, gpus) which might be rendered inconsistently.

References shared during call: - JW: link to "jp-region-benchmarks.xlsx" (Redwood internal) - SOW draft placeholder: /redwood/sow/sparrowline-pilot-draft-2028-03-19 (to be sent) - Security pack: /redwood/security/sparrowline-pack (will be attached)

End of file.
